tracks.d: Which buttons to press: ringing a sale, voids, discounts, refunds, split bills, end-of-day close, KDS screens, handhelds. Usually 1–2 sessions per person, often run by the installer. When it's done, a new hire can complete a basic sale without help. This is the part installers sell you.

How your business actually runs on the system: how orders flow at rush, who covers the till when it's slammed, what to do when the internet drops, how comps and voids get approved, how a return works on a busy Saturday. The installer doesn't know your rush — this part is yours to teach, and it's the part merchants skip. Budget it anyway.

warn: ⚠️ Merchants under-budget both. They'll budget the hardware to the dollar, then hand a new hire the terminal on a Friday night with no training. The fix is cheap next to the hardware — it's just paid hours. Plan them.

checklist: Everyone gets their own login PIN on day one — no shared logins, ever.
Run 10 practice sales per person before go-live: sale, void, discount, refund, split payment.
Learn the offline mode BEFORE the internet drops — where's the button, what still works.
Voids and refunds need a manager code — practice the call, not just the button.
Count float at open and close for the first two weeks — shortages surface fast.
End-of-day close: one person owns it, same steps, every night.
Write the 'when it breaks' card: who to call, what's the backup (spare terminal? paper slips?).
Week-one review: 15 minutes with each person — what confused them? Fix it now.
Practice returns and exchanges — they take 3× longer than sales when untrained.
Loyalty signup at the till: 20 seconds or skip it, don't hold the line.
cashier: Your PIN is you — every void, discount and refund traces to it. Never share it.
Card fails twice → change tender. Don't tap five times and hope.
Say the total out loud before they pay — catches mis-rings instantly.
Receipts: ask, don't assume. 'Receipt with you?'
If the line is 3+ deep, call for backup before it becomes 6.
Returns need the original receipt or ID — know which before they argue.
'Phone number for points?' — 5 seconds, every sale.
kitchen: No kitchen here — this is your back-room sheet. Same discipline applies.
Receive against the PO in the system — count it before you sign.
Damages go in the system the same day — not 'when I get to it'.
Put-away: the system's bin location is the law — 'I'll remember' fails.
Transfers between locations: scan out AND scan in.
Cycle counts: 15 minutes a day beats a full shutdown count.
Nothing hits the floor without a price in the system.
manager: End-of-day close is yours — same person, same steps, every night. No exceptions.
Voids, refunds, comps: approve in the moment — a pile of 'fix laters' is theft-adjacent.
User PINs: create on hire, disable on departure — same day.
Cash: count with the cashier present, both sign. Every time.
Offline mode drill: once a quarter, run the backup plan before you need it.
New hire: buddy them with your best cashier for 3 shifts — not your fastest, your most careful.
The 'when it breaks' card lives by the terminal — your number, the processor's number, the installer's number.
Price overrides need your code — track WHY, not just how much.
